missionPremise: pe-tokens.css states the PE line vocabulary by ROLE and is the authority on it: --ss-line-06 #414247 rules INSIDE a surface, --ss-line-14 #56575C the edge OF a surface, --ss-line-28 #8A8A8F focus / outline buttons / emphasis. SettingsModal.tsx painted ordinary structure with the emphasis token ten times and the shared raised Card edge made it eleven, so the Settings surface read white beside the workbench docks, which spell line06/line14 correctly. The operator reported it as too much white; the underlying fact is a misused semantic, not a taste call.
completionPredicate: Every line usage on the Settings surface carries the token its ROLE calls for, decided one occurrence at a time and reported with its reasoning; a file-shaped test pins the outcome and has been observed FAILING in both directions; tsc clean, full vitest green with the delta accounted for, chrome-kit gate exit 0; and the visual result is explicitly NOT claimed, because this repo has no screenshot harness.

The shared Card/Modal shell is INSIDE scope because the operator named the modal outer edge and the dispatch authorises a shared-shell change once the blast radius is reported. Dock, rail and map chrome are the stated reference and are untouched. principalFinding.headline: The line ladder is calibrated against the DOCK plane, but the Settings modal sits on the RAISED plane, where the semantically correct internal-rule token is effectively invisible.
principalFinding.instrument: scratchpad/contrast.mjs — WCAG contrast, self-tested 5/5 including one NOT-VACUOUS negative. Validated against an INDEPENDENT derivation: pe-tokens.css records, from a different author on a different date, that line-28 on the lifted --ss-raised measures 3.017. The instrument reproduces 3.017 exactly.
principalFinding.mechanism: This explains WHY the file was built the way it was. On the raised plane line06 disappears, so the author used line14 for internal rules and line28 for edges — a systematic one-rung shift to compensate for a lighter ground. Reasonable at the bottom, overshot at the top, where line28 is the brightest line in the palette and 75 points above the modal fill.
principalFinding.secondMechanismRejected: That SettingsModal was simply authored carelessly against the vocabulary. Rejected because careless authorship scatters, and this file was INTERNALLY consistent before the change: every edge line28, every rule line14, without exception. Consistency of that kind is a compensation, not a slip.
principalFinding.theDegradationIAmDECLARING: Assigning the role-correct token puts seven structural rules on line06 at 1.034 contrast against the modal fill, i.e. near-invisible. The Account row rules, the Connections and Team roster row rules, the tab strip underline, the ON THIS TAB divider and its footnote rule may all read as gone rather than as quiet. This is stated, not hidden.
principalFinding.whyIShippedItAnyway: Choosing line14 for a rule BECAUSE line06 is invisible would encode a palette defect into fifteen call sites, which is the write-a-fallback-so-it-does-not-raise pattern ENFORCEMENT bans. The raise is the correct behaviour. And the kit already ships this exact state one element higher: Modal.tsx:87 paints its header rule with line06 on the same ground and has shipped unremarked.
principalFinding.theRightFixIfTheEyeDisagrees: Palette-level, not a re-tune of these call sites: either a line step calibrated for --ss-raised, or dropping the modal fill from --ss-raised-98 to --ss-ink so the existing ladder lands. pe-tokens.css sets this precedent itself for the hover 7 percent — that is a palette-author question and belongs in a request, not in a re-tune here.

fleetMemory.entry: PE line tokens measured against each ground plane. On the MODAL ground --ss-raised-98 #3F4043: line06 1.034, line14 1.438, line28 3.017. On the DOCK ground --ss-ink #323234: line06 1.276, line14 1.775, line28 3.724. The ladder is calibrated for the dock plane; line06 is effectively invisible on the modal plane. Instrument self-tested against pe-tokens.css own independently recorded 3.017.

A surface that is INTERNALLY consistent but wrong against the vocabulary is a COMPENSATION, not carelessness. SettingsModal used line14 for every rule and line28 for every edge without exception — a systematic one-rung shift. Look for the ground it was compensating against before calling it a slip; here it was the lighter --ss-raised modal fill.

hauska-map PE: the modal outer edge is painted by components/Card.tsx (raised branch), NOT by components/Modal.tsx. Modal renders <Card raised>. Modal own line contribution is its header rule, already line06. Card has ONE importer (Modal), Modal has TWO (SettingsModal, PdfViewer). Do not go looking in Modal.tsx for the border.

In PE the shared shell is too NARROW to carry the modal convention: six modal-shaped surfaces exist and only two go through Card. PricingModal, CheckoutPage, UnlockCheckoutModal and SignUpCard hand-roll rModal + modalBg + shModal themselves. Any claim of the form fix-it-in-the-shell reaches 2 of 6. Enumerate by grepping PE.rModal / PE.shModal / PE.modalBg, never by grepping the component import.

Tie a token exemption to a PROPERTY of the call site, not to a count or a line number. Pinning one-line28-survives is presence-shaped and a new 1px border silently takes the slot. Pinning the surviving use must be `2px solid` is meaning-shaped: a structural 1px line cannot satisfy it. Prove it with a count-NEUTRAL violation (swap an edge with a rule so the totals are unchanged) — if that passes, the site pin is vacuous.

When verifying by violation in a lane that already has uncommitted work, snapshot the LANE working state to scratch and restore from THAT. git checkout would revert the lane work itself. Verify the restore with md5 against the snapshot and with git status, and state that the induced failures are excluded from the reported counts.

apps/property-explorer/scripts/pe-chrome-kit-gate.mjs is IMPORT-SAFE (guarded by process.argv[1] === import.meta.url) and EXPORTS stripComments, hasButtonImport, hasPeImport. Tests can reuse them instead of respelling. tsconfig EXCLUDES src/**/*.test.ts, so a test importing a .mjs is never type-checked by tsc.

hauska-map baseline at commit fbda04a: apps/property-explorer npx vitest run = 158 files / 2104 passed / 1 todo, tsc --noEmit exit 0, pe-chrome-kit-gate exit 0 with SELF-TEST 76/76 and coverage 87/87. Setup is pnpm install --prefer-offline at the ROOT then pnpm --filter @hauska/map-renderer build; without the renderer build the app does not resolve.

Do NOT read a strict fill-based reading of the line vocabulary as decisive. Applying edge-means-a-fill-change literally sends EVERY box in Settings to line06 (the Panel and the Team boxes have no background), which makes the whole surface ruleless. The kit has no token for an unfilled outlined group on the raised plane; treat such a group as the edge of a bounded region (line14) and say so, rather than following the fill test off a cliff.

--surface-border-soft is NOT a live defect. It has zero consumers repo-wide; only two definitions exist, one of them a stale v2 docs copy carrying #243247. Do not spend a lane renaming it expecting a visual change.
